references.text: The people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching. [ref:Jonah 3:5-10|Jonah 3:5-10] describes how the people in Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and turned from their evil ways, as Jesus refers to in this verse.

Jonah was sent to Nineveh to preach against the city. [ref:Jonah 1:1-2|Jonah 1:1-2] is the background for the mission that Jesus refers to when he says that the people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching.

[ref:Matt 12:41|Matthew 12:41] is the parallel passage where Jesus says the same thing: The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at Jonah's preaching, and now something greater than Jonah is here.
[ref:Matt 12:6|Matthew 12:6] expresses the same principle that something greater than the temple is here – Jesus repeatedly points to his own superiority over Old Testament types, including Jonah.

[ref:Luke 11:31|Luke 11:31] is the immediately preceding verse, where Jesus uses the parallel example of the queen of the South (Sheba) who came to hear Solomon's wisdom – and now something greater than Solomon is here.

[ref:Luke 11:29-30|Luke 11:29-30] provides the context for the statement: Jesus calls his contemporaries an evil generation that demands a sign, and says that the sign of Jonah is the only sign they will receive.

[ref:Rom 2:27|Romans 2:27] addresses the same principle that Gentiles who keep the law will condemn those who have the law but break it – parallel to how the people of Nineveh, a Gentile nation, will condemn Israel's generation.

[ref:Jer 3:11|Jeremiah 3:11] says that apostate Israel has shown itself more righteous than faithless Judah – a principle that other nations can stand as witnesses against God's people who do not repent.

[ref:Ezek 3:5-7|Ezekiel 3:5-7] states that foreign peoples would have listened to God's word, while the house of Israel would not listen – the same point Jesus makes about the people of Nineveh compared to his own generation.

[ref:Matt 11:21-24|Matthew 11:21-24] contains Jesus' statement that Tyre, Sidon, and Sodom would have repented if they had seen his miracles – the same theme of Gentile nations responding better than Israel.
